physics_gate_2.check_values_asserted: tests/test_physics.gd test_cmb: HB-62 38.44 K, HB-63 3,853.7 K, package pole 3853.7309940335736 K (1e-12), 1/gamma 1926.867102770845 K, 2/gamma 770.7475347575637 K, apparent 45 deg 0.0131574 K, apparent 90 deg T0/gamma 0.0038537 K, rest-frame 90 deg gamma T0 1926.8664604500 K at asin(1/gamma) = 0.0810 deg (HB-68), photopicRadiance 1.9842652619e8 / 290755.10 / 0.00275544 cd/m^2 and the package-doc 2856 K and 5772 K values; at rest 2.725 K everywhere and radiance exactly 0.
physics_gate_2.oracle_independent: Python (second language) from the spec's definitions, not from the package or GDScript: gamma(1e-6) = 707.1069579633; pole T0 gamma (1 + beta) = 3853.7309940336 K; naive 1 - beta cos theta' loses 3e-11 at the pole (the 1 - beta form is needed for the 1e-12 assertion; mutant M2 confirms); T at 1/gamma 1926.867 K, at 2/gamma 770.748 K, at apparent 90 deg 0.0038537 K; rest-frame 90 deg 1926.866 K at 0.08103 deg; gamma 275 pole 1498.75 K, HB-67 gamma(1500 K) = 275.23. photopicRadiance from 2hc^2 = 1.1910429723971884e-16 W m^2 sr^-1 (exact SI) x 683 lm/W on the Wyman-Sloan-Shirley ybar at 1 nm: 1.98426526e8 cd/m^2 at the pole (claim 1.98e8 ok), 7,673 cd/m^2 at gamma 275, 0.0076 at the Draper point gamma 146 (HB-64/65 consistent: a faint red glow). The oracle shares the ybar fit with the package (the package doc bounds it at 0.5% of CIE over 1,900-6,000 K, 1% at 800 K); it is independent in the Planck/photometric scale and the integration, not in the colour-matching model.
physics_gate_2.disc_size: Half-temperature radius 1/gamma = 4.86' at gamma 707 (claim 4.9' ok). The VISIBLE disc, where T0 D gives L above the 23.5 mag/arcsec^2 sky (4.33e-5 cd/m^2), has radius 10.5' = 2.17/gamma (T 675 K there); above 1e-3 cd/m^2 it is 9.9'. At gamma 275 the visible radius is 13.8' (1/gamma = 12.5'). So the 4.9' figure is the thermal core, and the disc the eye sees is about twice that; the executor's own CORE_CUT 1e-15 puts the profile edge at ~11.8' plus 9 sigma of PSF, theta_max ~1.1 deg, which is right.
physics_gate_2.disc_illuminance: integral 2 pi sin(theta) photopicRadiance(T0 D(theta)) dtheta = 188.73 lux at the cap (claim ~189 ok), 0.0197 lux at gamma 275. The blurred profile integrates to the same illuminance (test, 1e-12 and 1%).
physics_gate_2.lookup_table: 1025 entries over [0, 5000 K], log10 L linear in T, floor -60: all finite in the oracle and in the GDScript test; first entry above the floor at T ~127 K; log-linear interpolation errors at 700 / 1000 / 1499 / 2000 / 3000 / 3853.7 / 4999 K are 3.4e-4, 9e-5, 8e-7, 1.7e-5, 5e-6, 2e-6, 8e-7 (test limit 2e-3; a 65-entry table fails it, mutant M5c). Above 5000 K the exact function is used, so the range covers every speed up to the D-15 cap with margin (pole 3,853.7 K).
physics_gate_2.psf_sigma_6_arcmin: Defensible. Shlaer 1937 (J Gen Physiol 21:165) gives scotopic minimum angle of resolution of 10-20', and a Gaussian of FWHM 14' (sigma 6') sits inside that; at threshold it is really neural summation rather than optical blur, but for the purpose (star splat width, EV_dark constant) a Gaussian is the right engineering form. EV_dark = log2(E_thr / (2 pi sigma^2) / floor / 1.2) has no pixel term, so it is -4.40 at every size (test, exact); the 0.7 px clamp at 540 rows (6.2') costs 0.10 mag of V_lim, measured (6.8 at 960x540 golden, 6.9 at 2560x1440 bench), and the dark sky renders linear 7.63e-4 = 1/255 at both sizes (golden and bench lines). The M1.5a 7.1x resolution dependence is gone. Caveat: the dark-adapted sigma is also applied when the eye is light-adapted at EV +12 (photopic acuity ~1'), and the real ocular PSF at 2e8 cd/m^2 is dominated by wide-angle scatter (CIE glare function), which a 6' Gaussian under-represents; see finding 1.
physics_gate_2.meter: Sound as an adaptation-level model. L_eye = (sum w L Omega + sum w E') / sum w Omega with w = exp(-theta^2 / 2 (12 deg)^2) and pinhole cos^3 cell solid angles; point sources enter as seen illuminance E pointFluxRatio(T, D) = E Y(DT)/Y(T)/D^2 (I re-derived: I_nu/nu^3 invariant gives L' = L(DT), dOmega' = dOmega/D^2, so E' = E Y(DT)/Y(T)/D^2; the package form). The CMB enters as its integrated illuminance at the heading. Oracle: sum w Omega = 0.27068 sr at 70 deg and 0.00849 sr at 4 deg, so L_eye = 697 cd/m^2 (EV 12.45) and 22,238 cd/m^2 (EV 17.44); the captures print 696.7 and 22,219 (EV +12.44 / +17.44). The arithmetic mean is the right statistic (a log mean cannot see a point source). Physiologically EV 12.4 is an overcast-day adaptation and EV 17.4 a sunlit one; both are plausible mean-field adaptations and the zoom's higher level is physically right in direction (an optic of magnification M raises retinal illuminance ~M^2). What is NOT modelled: the disc itself is 1.98e8 cd/m^2 over a 20' disc, an eighth of the solar disc (1.6e9); discomfort glare for a point source on a dark surround starts near 1e4-1e5 cd/m^2 and photochemical retinal damage from the sun takes seconds to minutes of fixation, so at gamma 707 looking ahead through the dome is a glare and, with fixation, a retinal-hazard situation. D-15 shields UV/X-rays with glazing; a 3,854 K blackbody is visible and near-IR, so the glazing does nothing for this. A warning, a saturation/afterimage effect or auto-dimming glazing is a design decision for Mark, not something the executor should have invented; it is listed in next_steps as a ledger question.

findings.scope: sky/sky_meter.gd, sky/exposure.gd state_name(), main.gd hud; D-15 glazing
findings.title: The disc at gamma 707 is a glare and retinal-hazard source and nothing in the model, the HUD or the ledger says so
findings.detail: 1.98e8 cd/m^2 over a ~20' disc is an eighth of the solar disc. The eye model adapts the mean field to EV +12.4 (697 cd/m^2) and draws a clean dot; a real observer gets discomfort glare, an afterimage, and with fixation a photochemical lesion in minutes. The glazing ruled in D-15 absorbs UV/X, not 3,854 K visible light. This is the 'true adaptation model must come with M1.8' item from the M1.5a evaluation, half done. Not a physics error in M1.8's claims, so not blocking the milestone, but it belongs in front of Mark at R-e: HUD label ('blinding: disc 2e8 cd/m^2'), a saturation/afterimage effect, or auto-dimming dome glazing as lore. Recommend an OPEN ledger row.

findings.title: Two contracts covered only by captures or comments
findings.detail: The main-to-meter CMB wiring and the lookup range have no failing test when broken. Add a golden (or a physics check through a MainLoop stub) for the first and a one-line check for the second.

findings.title: The PSF is fixed in sky angle; at a zoomed field of view it should scale with the magnification
findings.detail: sigma = 6' of sky is the eye's blur only at the natural field of view; through a 70/4 = 17.5x optic the eye's 6' is 0.34' of sky. The 4 deg zoom renders are therefore ~17x too soft (the disc should show its 10.5' visible edge). Capture-only today; either document the zoom as a diagnostic or set sigma_sky = 6' x fov / 70.

findings.title: The camera frames' 3 deg halo is Godot glow on a 6e4-clamped pixel, not the CMB profile
findings.detail: theta_max of the profile is ~1.1 deg; the halo in the camera-auto/fixed frames is the post-process bloom of a saturated pixel. Fair as 'the camera cannot hold it' but uncalibrated; say so in the R-e note so the look is not read as physics.

findings.title: main.gd keeps growing against the M1.5a follow-up to shrink it
findings.detail: Move _capture_cmb, _capture_exposure_pair and the eye-meter cache into tools/capture.gd or sky/; a MainLoop-style split would also let the meter wiring be tested headless (finding 2).

findings.title: The dark-adapted sigma is used when the eye is light-adapted
findings.detail: At EV +12 the eye is photopic (acuity ~1') and its PSF is dominated by glare scatter; a single 6' Gaussian is the scotopic case. Acceptable for M1 (the star splat width is what it tunes); revisit with the glare model.

deviations.what: AC '1,926.9 K at theta' = 90 deg' asserted for the REST-FRAME 90 deg direction (which appears at asin(1/gamma) = 0.081 deg); at apparent 90 deg the CMB is T0/gamma = 0.0039 K
deviations.verdict: ACCEPT. The AC conflated the two frames; the package doc (optics.cmbSeenTemperature vs cmbSeenTemperatureApparent) and my oracle agree with the executor, both readings are asserted, and the Doppler convention D = 1/(gamma (1 - beta cos theta')) is the one in use throughout. Sideways at speed is redshifted.

deviations.what: Captures fly a real journey (new_game, plan, commit, boost, cruise) to reach gamma 275 and 707 instead of injecting a velocity
deviations.verdict: ACCEPT, better than the plan: it exercises the sim's cruise cap (D-15 cruise_phi_max gives gamma 707.0 at 1 - beta = 1e-6) and keeps the ship at Sol so the starfield is the familiar one; the HUD rows (ship 0.000 yr, travelled 0.001 ly) show the D-11 boost-in-minutes profile.

deviations.what: The 4 deg zoom re-meters the eye (EV +17.4 vs +12.4)
deviations.verdict: ACCEPT with finding 3. Re-adapting to a higher level through a magnifying optic is physically right in direction (more flux on the retina), and the EV reproduces from the meter's definition; the zoom's PSF should scale with the magnification, and the zoom should be labelled a diagnostic view, not a game view.
ACCEPT with a deduction (-2 code quality) and finding 5; the growth is 77 lines of capture driver and meter cache that belong elsewhere.

deviations.what: make bench p99 miss of 41-57 ms under host load 8-17, origin/main missing equally
deviations.verdict: ACCEPT as environmental, now verified: on a quiet host p99 is 9.67 ms (metal) / 9.57 ms (vulkan), 2 of ~3560 frames over 16.7 ms, V_lim 6.9, star pass 0.89 ms, with the eye meter running every 100 ms.

deviations.what: LOC ~823 raw (~709 counted) over the 650 cap, 300 estimated
deviations.verdict: ACCEPT with a deduction (-1 code quality). The overrun is the two follow-ups the M1.5a evaluation and the coordinator put 'before M1.8' (angular PSF, centre-weighted meter) plus ~200 lines of tests for them; they were sanctioned, not scope creep, and splitting them into their own PR would have cost a second GPU gate cycle. The plan's estimate should have been revised when they were folded in; counted LOC is 1.09x the cap, inside the plan's own '1.1x overrun still fits'.
